Cranberry Walnut Bread
by  Henry Hunter  • recipepantry.app
PREP TIME
30 minutes
FERMENTATION
20-26 hours
BAKE TIME
40-45 minutes
YIELD
1 loaf (about
1,100g), 12 slices
Tart cranberries pop against toasted walnuts with a crust that shatters when you slice it.
Ingredients
Levain (build night before)
50g  Active sourdough starter
100g  Water (80-85°F / 27-29°C)
100g  Bread flour

Dough
~250g  Levain (all of it)
375g  Water (80-85°F / 27-29°C)
500g  Bread flour
10g  Fine sea salt
75g  Dried cranberries
75g  Walnuts, toasted and coarsely chopped
Equipment
•  Large mixing bowl
•  Kitchen scale
•  Bench scraper
•  Banneton basket (or a bowl lined with a floured towel)
•  Dutch oven with lid (5 to 6 quart)
•  Lame or sharp knife
•  Parchment paper
•  Wire cooling rack
Instructions
1 .  Build Your Levain
Mix 50g active sourdough starter with 100g water (80-85°F) and 100g bread flour in a clean jar.
Stir until combined, cover loosely, and let sit at room temperature overnight. You want it bubbly
and doubled by morning, with a domed top.
1 .  Combine starter and water
Mix 50g active sourdough starter with 100g water (80-85°F) in a clean jar.
50g  Sourdough starter  100g  Water
2 .  Add flour
Add 100g bread flour and stir until combined.
3 .  Rest overnight
Cover loosely and let sit at room temperature overnight (8-10 hours). It should be bubbly and
doubled by morning.

2 .  Prepare Inclusions
Toast walnuts and soak cranberries before mixing your dough.
1 .  Toast walnuts
Spread walnuts on a baking sheet and toast at 350°F for 5-7 minutes until fragrant. Let cool
completely, then chop coarsely.
2 .  Soak cranberries
Soak dried cranberries in warm water for 15 minutes to plump them. Drain well and pat
completely dry with a towel.
3 .  Mix the Dough
Combine your levain with water and flour for the autolyse.
1 .  Dissolve levain
In a large bowl, add 375g water (80-85°F) and dissolve all of your levain into it.
~250g  Levain  375g  Water
2 .  Add flour
Add 500g bread flour and mix with your hands until no dry flour remains. The dough will look
shaggy and rough.
3 .  Autolyse
Cover and let rest for 45 minutes. This autolyse develops gluten without effort.
4 .  Add Salt and Develop Strength
Incorporate salt and begin building gluten structure.
1 .  Add salt
Sprinkle 10g salt over the dough.
2 .  Incorporate
Pinch and fold the dough repeatedly for about 5 minutes until the salt is fully incorporated and
the dough starts to tighten up.
3 .  Rest
Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

5 .  Stretch and Folds with Inclusions
Build strength and incorporate the cranberries and walnuts.
1 .  First set of folds
Wet your hand, grab one side of the dough, stretch it up, and fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl a
quarter turn and repeat 4 times total. Rest 30 minutes.
2 .  Test dough strength
Try pressing in a small handful of cranberries and walnuts. If the dough tears or goes slack, do
another set of folds, wait 30 minutes, then try again.
3 .  Add half the inclusions
If the dough holds together, add half your cranberries and walnuts and fold them in gently. Rest
30 minutes.
4 .  Second set of folds
Add the remaining cranberries and walnuts and do another round of stretch and folds. Rest 30
minutes.
5 .  Third set of folds
Final stretch and folds. The dough should feel smooth, strong, and slightly puffy.
6 .  Bulk Fermentation
Let the dough ferment at room temperature for about 4 to 5 hours total from mixing. Go by the
dough, not the clock: volume up about 50%, a domed top, bubbles visible under the surface, and a
finger indent that slowly springs back halfway.
1 .  Monitor fermentation
Cover and let ferment. Watch for 50% volume increase, visible bubbles, and dome formation.
2 .  Check readiness
Press a finger in. The indent should slowly spring back halfway. Trust what you see over the
clock.

Shape Your Loaf
Boule (Round)
1 .  Pre-shape
Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Preshape into a round by pulling edges toward
the center, creating tension on the surface.
2 .  Bench rest
Let rest 15-20 minutes uncovered (bench rest).
3 .  Final shape
Flip the dough so smooth side is down. Fold edges to center again, creating a tight ball. Flip
over and drag across counter to build surface tension.
4 .  Into banneton
Place seam-side up in a well-floured banneton or bowl lined with floured towel.
Bake Your Loaf
Temperature:  450 °F /  230 °C

IF USING:  DUTCH OVEN
1 .  Preheat
About 45 minutes before baking, place the Dutch oven with its lid in the oven and heat to 450°F
(230°C). Leave the loaf in the fridge until you're ready to load it.
2 .  Prepare loaf
Turn the cold loaf out onto parchment paper. Score the top with a lame or sharp knife. One
deep slash down the center works great.
3 .  Load Dutch oven
Carefully remove the hot Dutch oven, lower in the loaf (parchment and all), and cover with the
lid.
4 .  Steam bake
Bake covered at 450°F (230°C) for 20 minutes for oven spring.
5 .  Finish bake
Remove the lid, lower the oven to 425°F (220°C), and bake 20-25 minutes until deep golden
brown and the internal temperature reaches 205-210°F (96-99°C). The lower heat keeps the
cranberries and walnuts from scorching.
6 .  Cool
Transfer to a wire rack and cool for at least 1 hour before slicing. The crumb is still setting.
Storage
Room Temperature:  Store wrapped in a towel or in a bread bag for up to 3 days. The
cranberries and walnuts keep it moist.
Refrigerated:  Not recommended. Refrigeration accelerates staling.
Frozen:  Slice and freeze for up to 2 months. Toast frozen slices for breakfast or cheese
plates.
Refresh:  Warm slices in a 300°F oven for 5 minutes to refresh.

FAQ
Can I use fresh cranberries instead of dried?
Dried works better. Fresh cranberries add too much moisture and can make your dough too wet to
handle. If you must use fresh, pat them completely dry and reduce the amount to 50g maximum.
Do I have to use a Dutch oven?
A Dutch oven gives the best oven spring and crust, but you can bake on a stone with steam. Just
know your results will vary.
Why is my dough tearing when I add the inclusions?
You added them before the gluten was strong enough. Do more stretch and folds to build strength
first, then try again. The dough should feel elastic and hold together before you add heavy mix-ins.
How do I know when bulk fermentation is done?
Look for about a 50% volume increase, visible bubbles under the surface, a domed top, and a
dough that springs back slowly when poked.
My loaf didn't rise much in the oven. What happened?
Most often the dough was underproofed in bulk or overproofed in the fridge, or the starter wasn't
active enough. Check your starter first. It should double within 6 to 8 hours of feeding.
Can I skip the cold proof?
Yes. After shaping, proof at room temperature for 1 to 2 hours until a floured finger indent springs
back slowly, then bake the same way. The loaf will taste milder and be harder to score cleanly.
